data.gender_notes: Amrisha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Amrisha is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Amrut’, meaning ‘nectar’ or ‘immortal’. This name is often given to girls in Hindu culture to signify the everlasting nature of the soul. The name Amrisha carries the meaning “Immortal, Everlasting” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amrisha usually hope their child will grow to embody immortal, everlasting and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: May your life be filled with the nectar of happiness and love.
data.etymology: Amrisha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Immortal, Everlasting.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amrisha total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

In Hindu culture, Amrisha is often given to baby girls as a name that represents purity, grace, and the timeless quality of the soul. The name has a unique connection to Hindu mythology, particularly the tales of the gods and their quests for immortality.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual meaning of the name Amrisha holds immense significance in Hinduism. It is a reminder that despite the transient nature of our physical existence, our true self remains unchanged and unending. The name Amrisha can serve as a source of inspiration and motivation for individuals seeking to deepen their spiritual practices and connect with their inner selves.

historical_references.reference: Amrisha was the name of the eldest daughter of the legendary king Harshavardhana (600-647 CE) of the Hindu kingdom of Thanesar in present-day Haryana, India.
historical_references.context: Harshavardhana was a prominent ruler in early medieval India, known for his patronage of arts, culture, and religion. His court was a melting pot of diverse traditions and ideas.

historical_references.reference: Amrisha is also the name of a queen who lived in the 13th century CE, during the reign of the Yadava dynasty in the Deccan region of India. She is known for her role in the construction of the famous cave temples at Ellora.
historical_references.context: The Ellora caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site, showcasing the architectural brilliance and cultural richness of ancient India. Queen Amrisha is believed to have contributed significantly to this architectural marvel.
